newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies close at day's highs.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies close at day's highs.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures ran up on fundamental and technical demand to end at the day's highs and highest levels since early October, traders said.

Hog futures finished 0.800 cent a lb higher to 0.100 lower with December up most at 57.500 cents, the highest level since October 10. Pork bellies ended 1.800 cent a lb higher to 0.025 lower with February up 1.575 at 74.475 cents, the highest since October 11.

Firm cash markets kept hog futures supported and prices ran up to the highs late on closing buy stops, traders said. Although demand for hogs may ease next week, the overall trend appears to be tighter hog supplies, traders said.

"We have a strong fundamental picture, but it looks like we will cut the kills somewhat next week. Packers will try to pay a little bit less for hogs next week, but the supply side is fairly sound," said Karl Skold, director of research for Frontier Risk Management.
Skold and other analysts expect reduced hog supplies to end the year, especially with producers starting to hold some hogs out of the market mix for breeding purposes.
"We are going to end up with reduced kills as we march through the last half of November into December," Skold added.

Even though December futures hold a large premium to current cash prices, cash strength has encouraged the bullish longer-term fundamental ideas. Interior hog marketings have been lighter and cash pork prices are showing continued strength, partly from increased exports, traders said.
CME December hog futures closed Friday at 57.500 cents a lb versus cash hog prices in direct Midwest trade at $53.00 to $54.50 Friday, with the top paid in Iowa trade.

The recent lighter slaughter pace has also buoyed cash belly prices and in turn, added to a strong technical picture in pork belly futures to lift prices to a one-month high. Higher prices are needed to encourage storings, they said.
"Given our (low) freezer position, that is going to support bellies too," Skold said of the smaller slaughter.
USDA estimated this week's hog slaughter at 1,832,000 head, below 1,851,000 a week ago and 1,981,000 a year ago.
Analysts noted that hog slaughter was running seven percent under last year while indications from the last USDA Hogs and Pigs report had pointed to a four percent reduction.
Refco bought hogs late and closing buy stops offset long fund rolling into February. Cargill Investor Services was the notable buyer in pork bellies late, pit sources said.

In hog options, volatility in December was under further pressure while February was firm. There was scattered buying up October 64 calls and strangle buying in February, buying 75 puts and selling 80 calls, pit sources added.
